correctness.rationale: The four cases cover all n>=3 of support size at most five. Even mixed supports force 6|psi(n), so phi(psi(n))/psi(n)<=1/3, and strict monotonicity of 1+1/p bounds psi(n)/n by 1152/385. Equality requires both the first five primes and no prime outside {2,3} in psi(n); the prime-power formula forces exponents 1 at 5,7,11 and allows any positive exponents at 2,3. Remaining cases give 1/2, 512/715 and 20480/22971, each strictly smaller. Direct computation gives psi(39270)=124416 and its totient 41472; it shows failure is possible at six factors, not that every six-factor input fails. At n=2 the composition equals 2. The independently written /workspace/reproduction/independent_5.py uses exact trial division and reproduced 299731 eligible inputs, 22 equality cases and 23 violations (first 39270) up to 300000; the unbounded result rests on the proof, not the finite run.

originality.rationale: Demonstrably covered by a mechanical sharpening of the already published October 12 five-support barrier proof. Its actual proof, not just its stated theorem, gives the exact bounds 1/3 and 1152/385 for the two factors of the even ratio. It also already bounds the odd branches by (1/2)(4608/2431) and (1/3)(1536/715), both strictly below 384/385. Multiply the displayed bounds and inspect equality in those same two even products: the five smallest primes are necessary, and no other primes than 2 and 3 may divide psi(n); the prior prime-power formula gives exactly the stated equality family. The prior record already gives the very same six-prime counterexample. No new inequality or case estimate is needed for the assigned sharp global result. The same-date six-support record supplies parallel overlap but is not needed to infer priority.
residual_risks: Das (2023), On Sandor's conjecture; Alzer–Kwong (2020), Inequalities for the arithmetical functions of Euler and Dedekind; and Sándor's unpublished 1988 notes were not verified in full.
